Inigo Jones surveys Stonehenge for James I; also first known excavation in the centre, led by the Duke of Buckingham, in the 1620s. Jones's plan (published 1655 by Webb) is a symmetrical Roman restoration, not a record of the stones' real state. Exact survey year: not confirmed from a fetched source (snippet says 1610s commission; EH says 1620s).
AFTER TIMELINE NOTE: John Aubrey surveys the site and records the ring of pits later called the Aubrey Holes
AFTER TIMELINE: southwest trilithon (57-58 and lintel 158) falls; re-erected 1958. So it stood in 1625 (inference).

AFTER TIMELINE: stone 22 falls 31 December with its lintel; stone 23 re-erected 1963 (Wikipedia wording ambiguous); stone 56 straightened 1901; stone 60 straightened 1959; last consolidation 1964. Stones standing in 1625 by inference unless earlier plans show otherwise.

Stone robbing: Wikipedia says stones were taken for building until the 17th century and tourists chipped souvenirs in the 19th. No dated robbing event, no named stone taken before 1625 found in fetched sources. Darvill: sockets of stones 13 and 20 recorded, so robbed in historic times (inference).

completenessDebate: Missing in the SW: uprights 13, 17, 18, 20, 24 and about 24 lintels (Darvill 2012). Ashbee (1998) argued the circle was never completed; Darvill considers historic robbing more likely because the sockets of 13 and 20 are recorded. Banton et al. 2014 (Antiquity 88: 733-739) report July 2013 drought parchmarks between stones 16 and 21 interpreted as stoneholes where expected uprights should be (Daw, an author, says evidence the circle was 'intended' complete, not that it was); the abstract page I could read says only that the parchmarks 'provide more evidence' and that expected stones are missing; the stone-hole detail is from search snippets. Press (Greaney, EH): 'if these stone holes actually held upright stones then we've got a complete circle'. Net: unresolved; for the 1625 model treat the SW arc as a gap with a low-confidence 'was never there / was robbed' choice and record it as such.
